'''Deal With It!''' is [[Richard Handley|Rich Handley]]'s report in ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' #52 (pages 68–69) on [[DecipherCon 2000]] and its [[2000 Decipher World Championship|Star Wars CCG World Championship]].<ref name="swi52" /><ref name="wook-52" /> Its subtitle is "It's a CCG TKO When Star Wars Fans Compete at DecipherCon 2000". The issue went on sale on 27 February 2001.<ref name="wook-52" />

[[File:Star Wars Insider 52 page 68.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Star Wars Insider #52, page 68.]]
[[File:Star Wars Insider 52 page 69.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Star Wars Insider #52, page 69.]]

== Star Wars CCG World Championship ==
DecipherCon 2000 ran on 5–8 October 2000 at the Doubletree Resort and Conference Center in Kissimmee, Florida.<ref name="swi52" /> The Star Wars CCG tournament drew 72 players. The final matched [[Yannick Lapointe]] of Montreal, Canada, against [[Matt Sokol]] of Albany, New York.<ref name="swi52" />

In Game 1 Lapointe played a [[Bring Him Before Me / Take Your Father's Place|Bring Him Before Me]] deck. Sokol played a space deck built on [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers|Hidden Base]]. He forgot to include the Luke card it needed and lost by 20.<ref name="swi52" /> In Game 2 Lapointe played a [[Mind What You Have Learned / Save You It Can|Mind What You Have Learned]] Jedi-training deck. He activated all his Force without a reserve deck, and Sokol's Dark Side deck won the game and the title.<ref name="swi52" />

Sokol's win was the first American Star Wars CCG world title since [[Matt Potter]] in 1998. It was Lapointe's third World Championship.<ref name="swi52" /> The two had often played each other since meeting at the Ottawa Grand Slam. Sokol said: "I'm going to DisneyWorld!"<ref name="swi52" />

== Young Jedi World Championship ==
Seventy players entered the [[Young Jedi]] World Championship. A dozen finalists played constructed decks. Ian Vincent of Hastings, England, beat [[Philippe Parise|Philippe Parrise]] of Ontario, Canada, in the final.<ref name="swi52" />

In Game 1 Parrise's Anakin deck beat Vincent's tank deck by 19. The two swapped decks for Game 2, and Vincent won it by 26 to take the title.<ref name="swi52" /> Vincent had placed seventh in the previous year's Star Trek CCG finals.<ref name="swi52" />

Other Young Jedi finalists as printed: 3 [[James Lafferty]] (California), 4 Jeremy Baker, 5 [[Benoit Morel]], 6 [[Avery Poliak|Avery Pollak]], 7 [[Tom Mascari]], 8 Jennifer Ekstrom, 9 [[Jonathan Swenson]], 10 Adam Fuentez, 11 Irina Nepevna and 12 [[Jeff Kahan]].<ref name="swi52" />

== Guests and other events ==
The convention introduced the DecipherCon Olympics, a three-day event of card-sorting, card-house-building and card-tossing. Players attended seminars on card design and DigitalDeck's online card game. They also saw the new [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]].<ref name="swi52" />

[[Shannon Baksa]] and [[Michonne Bourriague]] signed comics, photographs and cards. Baksa had first attended the year before, after the Mara Jade card. She said: "Everyone here is so nice, and I love to be Mara!"<ref name="swi52" /> Bourriague, Aurra Sing in ''The Phantom Menace'', said: "It's been so wonderful being able to say I was in Star Wars."<ref name="swi52" /> Fans also saw Chronicle Books' ''Aurra Sing: Dawn of the Bounty Hunters'' with its 12-inch Aurra Sing figure.<ref name="swi52" />

== Discrepancies ==

Where a source disagrees with the record on the article, the article keeps the record and notes the difference here.

* Decipher's Young Jedi semifinal results list places 3rd to 12th in a different order from the ''Insider''.<ref name="dc-yj3">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/youngjedi3.html Young Jedi Finalists], Decipher (DecipherCon 2000 semifinal results). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020421134943/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/youngjedi3.html Internet Archive].</ref> Three places agree: Lafferty 3rd, Ekstrom 8th and Fuentez 10th. The other seven differ:
** Jeremy Baker: 4th in the ''Insider'', 12th on Decipher's page.<ref name="dc-yj3" />
** Jonathan Swenson: 9th in the ''Insider'', 4th on Decipher's page.<ref name="dc-yj3" />
** Irina Nepevna: 11th in the ''Insider'', 5th on Decipher's page.<ref name="dc-yj3" />
** Benoit Morel: 5th in the ''Insider'', 6th on Decipher's page.<ref name="dc-yj3" />
** Jeff Kahan: 12th in the ''Insider'', 7th on Decipher's page.<ref name="dc-yj3" />
** Avery Poliak: 6th in the ''Insider'' (printed "Avery Pollak"), 9th on Decipher's page.<ref name="dc-yj3" />
** Tom Mascari: 7th in the ''Insider'', 11th on Decipher's page.<ref name="dc-yj3" />
* Decipher's page spells the runner-up "Philippe Parrise", as the ''Insider'' does; this wiki's page is [[Philippe Parise]].<ref name="dc-yj3" />
